text: There was ink worn into the side of {his} second finger, too deep to scrub out, and sleeve guards folded in {his} breast pocket in case a column broke out.

trait.text: ink worn into the side of one finger, too deep to scrub out
pay: The ink worn into that finger would never scrub out. Mine, from the notebook, would by morning. That’s the difference between a career and a night.

text: {He} was neat in a way that took effort: every button done, the collar pinned, the hair flat. The hands stayed folded until {he} needed one, and then only the one.

trait.text: hands that stayed folded until one was needed, and then only the one
pay: One of those folded hands came unfolded, set something straight, and folded away again. I’ve seen banks spend less carefully.

text: A slight squint stayed with {him} even in good light, from years of adding small figures under a green lamp. It added me up once, and I came out short.

trait.text: a squint from years of adding small figures under a green lamp
pay: The squint added me up once more, in case it had forgotten to carry a one. I still came out short.

text: {He} smelled faintly of clove oil, and {his} hands were very clean and very steady. I kept my own mouth closed, on principle.

trait.text: hands that were very clean and very steady
pay: I kept my mouth shut, on principle. Those steady hands looked like they could have it open in a minute and a half.

text: {He} wore a starched white collar and a dark suit a little warm for the room, and {his} eyes went to my mouth the moment I came in. I had the feeling my fillings were being counted.

trait.text: eyes that went straight to my mouth
pay: Those eyes went back to my mouth, and I kept it closed. I didn’t want to hear how many fillings they’d counted.

text: {He} had the pale indoor look of somebody who spends the day bent over a chair under an electric light.

trait.text: the pale indoor look of somebody bent over a chair all day under an electric light
pay: Under the electric light we both looked like we’d spent the day bent over something. In my case it was the bar.

text: {He} was neat as a typed page, with a steno pad in {his} lap that {he} kept ready in case I said something worth taking down. So far {he} hadn’t needed it.

trait.text: a steno pad kept ready in case I said something worth taking down
pay: The steno pad was still blank. I’ve had reviews like that.

text: {He} had a way of waiting, head a little on one side, the way a person waits for dictation, and I found I was minding my grammar before I’d said a word.

trait.text: a way of waiting, head on one side, as if for dictation
pay: With that head tilted for dictation, I said nothing, and said it grammatically. It’s harder than it sounds.

text: {He} had fingertips gone flat from typing all day, and was dressed for an office in a good plain way that no office would ever notice.

trait.text: fingertips gone flat from typing all day
pay: The flat fingertips were typing on nothing, a line at a time. Nobody was dictating.

text: A press card was tucked in {his} hatband, and {he} looked at everything as if it might be worth two hundred words. I seemed to be worth about fifty.

trait.text: a press card tucked in the hatband
pay: The press card was still in the hatband. I was still worth about fifty words, and none of them were going on the front page.

text: {He} was a day past a shave and knew it, and the coat had the creases of somebody who had slept in a precinct chair.

trait.text: a chin a day past its shave
pay: I rubbed my own chin. It was two days past a shave, and I didn’t even have a deadline to blame.

text: {He} talked fast and wrote while {he} talked, on the back of whatever was handy, and never once looked down to see if it could be read.

trait.text: a pencil that wrote on whatever was handy without anybody looking
pay: The pencil was still going. I hoped it was spelling my name right. Nobody ever does.

text: {He} had a pianist’s back, bolt upright, and hands that seemed to be waiting to be counted in.

trait.text: hands that seemed to be waiting to be counted in
pay: Those hands were still waiting to be counted in. I nearly gave them a one-two-three myself, just to get things started.

text: One button was missing from the cardigan, and the music case had its handle mended with twine. Scales pay about what you’d think.

trait.text: a music case with its handle mended with twine
pay: The twine on the music case was holding. Most things in this city are held together with less.

text: {He} had long, cold-looking fingers and a habit of humming under {his} breath, always the same few bars and never the end of them.

trait.text: a habit of humming the same few bars and never the end of them
pay: The humming stopped short of the end again. I’d have paid a nickel to hear how it came out.

text: {He} had pins stuck in {his} collar where {he} could reach them, a thimble callus on one finger, and an eye on my loose button.

trait.text: an eye for a loose button
pay: I did my coat up over the loose button. It knew it had been seen.

text: Thin, and bent at the shoulders from years over a sewing machine, {he} wore clothes too good to have been bought. {He}’d made every stitch.

trait.text: clothes better made than anything a store sells
pay: I buttoned my coat. It came off a rack, and in that company it knew it.

text: {He} squinted at me the way you squint at a needle’s eye, and {he} doubted I’d go through.

trait.text: a squint for a needle’s eye
pay: The needle’s-eye squint stayed on me a while. I tried to look thinner. It didn’t help.

text: {He} had a driver’s cap with a shiny peak and a driver’s squint, and leaned forward wherever {he} was, as though stuck behind a streetcar.

trait.text: a way of leaning forward, as if stuck behind a streetcar
pay: Still that forward lean, as if stuck behind a streetcar. Somebody should have honked.

text: Heavy in the seat and quick with {his} eyes, {he} jingled change in one pocket, and somewhere a meter was running.

trait.text: change jingling in one pocket
pay: The change was still jingling. Somewhere a meter was running, and I had a feeling it was on me.

text: {He} smelled of gasoline and cold coffee and kept {his} gloves on indoors, the fingertips cut out of them.

trait.text: gloves with the fingertips cut out
pay: I could have used gloves with the fingertips cut out. Mine have all ten, and they still let the cold in.

text: {He} held {his} head tilted a little, as if the headset were still on it, and looked at me as if I were a call that had come through on the wrong line.

trait.text: a head tilted as if the headset were still on it
pay: The head was still tilted as if under a headset, listening. I kept quiet. I didn’t want to be put through to anybody.

text: {He} had quick small hands with the nails cut short for the plugs, and they kept tapping on {his} knee, still putting calls through to nobody.

trait.text: quick small hands still putting calls through to nobody
pay: The hands were still putting calls through. I hoped one of them was for me. Nobody had rung all week.

text: Young and tidy and a little tired, {he} still had the mark of the headset band pressed into {his} hair.

trait.text: the mark of the headset band pressed into the hair
pay: The headset band had left its mark in that hair, and my hat had left one in mine. Nobody was paying me by the hour for mine.

text: {He} had a cigar {he} wasn’t smoking and a folded racing sheet in {his} breast pocket, and did sums on {his} fingers without moving {his} lips. From the look of it, I was long odds.

trait.text: sums done on the fingers without moving the lips
pay: The fingers were still doing sums. From the look of it, my odds hadn’t got any shorter.

text: Round and pleasant and dressed a little too well for a cigar store, {he} kept {his} eyes on the door, in case it was the police or a winner.

trait.text: eyes on the door, in case it was the police or a winner
pay: The door opened. It was neither the police nor a winner. It hardly ever is, which is how bookmakers stay in business.

text: There was chalk on the side of one hand from a slate, and {he} kept wiping it on {his} trousers, which had given up.

trait.text: chalk from a slate, wiped off on the trousers
pay: A bit more chalk went on the trousers. They took it the way I take most things: without comment and without improving.

text: A jeweler’s glass hung on a ribbon round {his} neck, and {he} had a habit of turning things upside down to see the bottom.

trait.text: a habit of turning things upside down to see the bottom
pay: I kept both feet on the floor. In that company, anything could get turned upside down to see what was on the bottom.

text: {He} was thin and pale from the shop, a green eyeshade pushed up on {his} forehead, with the look of somebody who had heard every sad story on the block and priced them.

trait.text: a green eyeshade pushed up on the forehead
pay: I had a sad story of my own, but I kept it away from the green eyeshade. I didn’t want to hear what it would fetch.

text: My watch got looked at before I did. I could see {him} putting a figure on it, and the watch did better.

trait.text: an eye that put a figure on my watch
pay: I put my watch in my pocket. There’s no sense being outvalued by your own watch in public.

text: {He} was big and square and quiet, with a flattened nose and a collar a size too small for {his} neck. Most things were.

trait.text: a collar a size too small for the neck
pay: The collar was holding, just. So was I.

text: Hands clasped in front, weight back on {his} heels, {he} stood as though poured in place and left to set.

trait.text: a stance like something poured and left to set
pay: That poured-and-set stance hadn’t moved an inch. I walked round it.

text: {He} had scarred knuckles and a mild voice, and when I came in {he} looked at the door behind me, working out which of us would go through it easier.

trait.text: a look at the door, working out who would go through it easier
pay: I stayed a good way from the door. There was no sense helping anybody work out how easily I’d go through it.

text: {He} was young and quick and restless, and {his} pockets bulged with folded slips of paper that {he} kept a hand over and would have sworn were nothing.

trait.text: pockets that bulged with folded slips of paper
pay: A hand went over the bulging pockets again. I hadn’t asked. I hadn’t needed to.

text: {He} had a good hat and cheap shoes, and was up on {his} toes the whole time, ready to be somewhere else.

trait.text: a way of staying up on the toes, ready to be somewhere else
pay: The toes were still ready to be somewhere else. So were mine, but mine were further from the door.

text: {He} had a pencil stub behind {his} ear and small quick eyes that counted the room, then counted the ways out of it.

trait.text: small quick eyes that counted the ways out
pay: I counted the ways out myself. There were two, and one of them was the way I’d come in.

text: {He} had forearms like a baker’s and a clean towel over one shoulder, and wiped the bar after every glass, including the ones that hadn’t left a ring.

trait.text: a towel over one shoulder and a habit of wiping the bar after every glass
pay: The towel went down the bar once more, over a ring that wasn’t there. I’d been in cleaner places. I couldn’t think where.

text: Between customers {he} leaned on both hands spread on the bar, the way somebody leans who has been standing since the afternoon and has opinions about it.

trait.text: both hands spread on the bar
pay: The hands went back down on the bar. Standing since the afternoon, and not a word of complaint. I’ve complained about less by lunchtime.

text: {He} had a pleasant, forgettable face, which in that trade is the whole trick, and eyes that went to the door every time it opened, and came back.

trait.text: eyes that went to the door every time it opened, and came back
pay: Somebody came in behind me. The eyes went to the door and came back, and I was glad to see I’d been promoted to furniture.

text: {He} was tall in a long coat with brass buttons and a cap with a shiny peak, and stood very straight, as though the building might lean on {him}.

trait.text: a way of standing very straight, in case the building leaned
pay: That straight back was still braced in case the building leaned. The building didn’t. I did, a little, and nobody held me up.

text: {He} had a doorman’s face, pleasant and closed at once, and white gloves {he} started taking off a finger at a time when {he} saw me coming. I nearly left before the second glove.

trait.text: white gloves that came off a finger at a time
pay: The second glove was nearly off. I decided to stay for it. A man should see something finished.

text: Heavy in the coat and light on {his} feet, {he} had the door swung wide before I’d reached for it, and shut again before I’d decided anything.

trait.text: a way of having the door open before anybody reached for it
pay: I could feel the door behind me, ready to swing wide the moment I turned. It’s nice to be wanted gone that efficiently.

text: {He} had a roll of tickets on a spindle and a coin changer on {his} belt, and a callus on one thumb from tearing stubs, the only part of the job that showed.

trait.text: a callus on one thumb from tearing stubs
pay: The thumb with the callus was twitching for a stub. I didn’t have one. I rarely have a ticket for anything.

text: The uniform coat had the theater’s name on the collar, and the cap had been reshaped by a hundred hot nights.

trait.text: a cap reshaped by a hundred hot nights
pay: That uniform cap had been reshaped by a hundred hot nights. My own hat had had a few nights of its own, and not hot ones.

text: In the lit doorway {he} kept a hand out and didn’t look at faces, only at hands. I kept mine out of sight and felt rude.

trait.text: a hand held out, and eyes only for hands
pay: The hand was still out. I kept mine in my pockets and felt like a man without a ticket, which I was.

text: {He} had a big ring of keys at {his} waist and reading glasses pushed up into {his} hair, and looked at my shoes before my face, to see what they’d do to the stairs.

trait.text: a look at my shoes before my face, to see what they’d do to the stairs
pay: I wiped my feet, late. It didn’t do much for me, but the stairs appreciated it.

text: {He} was a stout woman in a housedress and cardigan, sleeves pushed up, with a dish towel over one shoulder for drying things, or swatting them.

trait.text: a dish towel over one shoulder, for drying things or swatting them
pay: The dish towel stayed on the shoulder. I stayed out of its reach, to be on the safe side.

text: {He} had strong hands, a sharp mouth, and a way of folding {his} arms that ended any conversation, especially one about the rent.

trait.text: a way of folding the arms that ended a conversation
pay: The arms were still folded. I felt in my pocket for the rent, out of habit. It isn’t even my building.

text: {He} wore a white coat with a fountain pen clipped in the pocket and rimless glasses on a chain, and {his} hands smelled of camphor. So, faintly, did the whole shop, and after a minute so did I.

trait.text: hands that smelled of camphor
pay: I smelled faintly of camphor by then, the only thing I’ve ever got from a drugstore for free.

text: {He} was the kind of druggist who didn’t look up from the brass scale until it balanced, and then looked at me as if I might tip it.

trait.text: a brass scale that had to balance first
pay: Somewhere behind the counter the brass scale settled. I wished something in my evening would.

text: Neat and gray and precise, {he} wrote everything down, and I had the feeling I’d be written down too before long.

trait.text: a habit of writing everything down
pay: The pen was still going. Whatever I’d done so far, it was in a book now, spelled right.
